summary: South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 26 covers November 1947, prepared by the National Economic Board for USAMGIK. The month opened with the inauguration of Maj. Gen. William F. Dean as Military Governor (3 November) after Lerch's death, and was dominated politically by the controversy over the Korean directors' 'Outline of Measures for Meeting the Current Situation', the UN-supervised election question, disputes between the executive and the Interim Legislative Assembly, and the Council of 12 Parties. Economic sections report a worsening coal and electric power crisis (58 trains cancelled, power cut from the North), half-complete rice collection, rising prices (index 1,476 in October), a 9.2 billion won note-issue increase, refugee inflows and housing, and detailed production, trade, transport, communications and finance tables. Social sections cover public health, the New Education Exhibit, culture and radio, public information, and Korean National Youth. A historian will find the primary-source text of the Outline, KILA debates, Ordinance 153/156 and the Beverage Tax ordinance, plus Radio Pyongyang monitoring.
highlights: Maj. Gen. William F. Dean was inaugurated Military Governor of South Korea on 3 November, succeeding the late Maj. Gen. Archer L. Lerch, and restated three aims: independent Korea, democratic government, and a sound economy and education system.

The 25 September 'Outline of Measures for Meeting the Current Situation in South Korea', signed by Ahn Chai Hong and Chough Pyung Ok, provoked leftist and rightist protest; KILA spent six sessions on it, rejected withdrawal 32 to 20, and Ahn said 'sovereign power' should read 'governing power'.

Hodge (19 November) and Dean (27 November) refused demands for a unilateral South Korean election before the UN Commission arrived; Rhee's National Society pressed for an election by mid-December while the Council of 12 Parties urged a North-South leaders' conference and lost members.

Coal and power shortages forced the removal of 58 trains from service; load reached 162,000 kw on 10 November against 105,000 kw available, 135,000 kw of it from north of the 38th parallel, and Chung Pyung, Unam and Sunjin Gang plants stopped for lack of water.

The Bank of Chosun note issue rose 9.2 billion won in November, the largest monthly rise since August 1946, driven by rice collection loans and deficit spending; the 1947/48 budget stood 45 per cent above 1946/47.

Rice collection was only half complete on 30 November, lagging in Cholla-pukto; 9,476,000 people were on rations at 2.5 hop (1,316 calories) a day, and the composite price index for 26 commodities reached 1,476 against August 1945 = 100.

Refugee arrivals from north of the 38th parallel were 7,715 in November, 155,454 for 1947 to date; total inbound movement since October 1945 was 2,350,133, and the report analysed the 1945, 1946 and 1947 migrations.

KILA passed the Temporary Law for Cessation of Professional Entertainment Activities, the Military Governor signed the Public Prostitution Law (Public Act No. 7), and Deputy Governor Helmick withheld approval of the Temporary Constitution and the collaborators' bill; Education Director Yu Uck Kyum died on 8 November.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Google Books notice, cover of No. 26 (November 1947, prepared by the National Economic Board, call number M 105.13:26), and the six-page table of contents for Parts I-VI.

sections.title: Part I. Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Population movements (2,350,133 inbound since 1945, 7,715 refugees in November), foreign affairs with China, Japan and the U.S., and vested property operations, loans, sales and Ordinance 156.

sections.title: Section 1. Population and Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: Reports repatriation and refugee totals, the 1945-47 migration pattern from the North, and Office of Foreign Affairs work on Chinese, Japanese and U.S.-European matters.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Introduces the Office of Foreign Affairs record of repatriates and refugees entering South Korea.

sections.title: Repatriation
sections.summary: Cumulative movement since 15 October 1945: 885,785 outbound, 2,350,133 inbound including 1,110,544 Koreans from Japan; SS Kaiwo Maru returned 509 illegal entrants on 7 November.

sections.title: Refugees
sections.summary: Monthly refugee counts (7,715 in November, 155,454 in 1947) and origins by province; explains the 1945 Manchurian flood, 1946 seasonal migration, and the 1947 refugee movement attributed to Sovietization.

sections.title: Chinese Affairs
sections.summary: 155 travel permits for Chinese nationals, SS Kim Kiu Jhan sailing for Tientsin and Shanghai, Manchurian refugee relief, and 11,126 registered Chinese in Korea.

sections.title: Japanese Affairs
sections.summary: Suspension of residence permits for Japanese wives of Koreans, 39 Japanese retained in essential posts, re-entry clearances, and recovery of Korean property and vessels from Japan.

sections.title: U.S. - European Affairs
sections.summary: Six Korean students left for the United States in November; papers for 39 others were in process.

sections.title: Section 2. Vested Property
sections.summary: Office of Property Custody handled 184 cases, reopened the Taichong gold mine, guaranteed loans, had 2,345 enterprises assigned to agents, and received Ordinance 156 on stockholders' meetings.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Notes that reporting on Property Custody operations remains only partial pending completion of operations under way.

sections.title: Operations
sections.summary: Operations Division handled 184 cases; Taichong Gold Mine reopening approved (4,200 grams estimated early 1948); timber land survey begun; table of loans guaranteed in November.

sections.title: Property Disposal
sections.summary: Sales and appraisals of vested property in November; Materials Control Corporation absorbed under Ordinance No. 155; provincial buyer-selection committees nearly complete.

sections.title: Assignment of Responsibility
sections.summary: 2,345 industrial and financial enterprises had been assigned to government department directors acting as agents of the Property Custodian.

sections.title: Ordinance No. 156
sections.summary: Text of Ordinance 156, published 21 November, empowering the Property Custodian to call stockholders' meetings on 30 days' notice.

sections.title: Current Activities
sections.summary: Rice-polishing mills leased by the Department of Commerce, Li Household income petition and audit, and changed eviction policy for unauthorized occupants.

sections.title: Administrative Problems and Decisions
sections.summary: Real estate handling by departments and banks, and a decision that shares in vested property are vested legally rather than administratively.

sections.title: General Counsel Division
sections.summary: Suits by Korean nationals against corporations holding vested Japanese shares, with jurisdictional defenses.

sections.title: Provincial Affairs Division
sections.summary: Rental control procedure to operate in all provinces by 31 January 1948; banks asked to report leasing breakdowns.

sections.title: Repair Funds Advanced
sections.summary: Table of Property Custody funds advanced for repairs, June to November 1947 and January-November totals.

sections.title: Part II. Production and Supply
sections.summary: Food supply and rationing, price indexes, agriculture, coal and metals, industrial output, allocation, trade and labor in November 1947, with the coal and grain shortages as main themes.

sections.title: Section 1. Food Supply
sections.summary: Summer grains nearly exhausted; 9,476,000 people rationed at 2.5 hop daily; rice collection half done, with Cholla-pukto lagging for lack of inspectors, trucks and bags.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Four-point summary of end-November food position: summer grains gone, small producers' rice stocks falling, imported grain supply uncertain.

sections.title: The Situation
sections.summary: Outlook pessimistic but no immediate starvation; stocks of non-rice grains and pulses close to exhaustion, with table of grain status 30 September-30 November.

sections.title: Imports
sections.summary: November grain imports near the monthly average, a little over 40 per cent of the tonnage distributed.

sections.title: Rationing
sections.summary: Rationed population unchanged at 9,476,000 of over 20 million; ration of 2.5 hop (1,316.2 calories) daily.

sections.title: The Rice Program
sections.summary: Collection one-half complete at 30 November, Cholla-pukto furthest behind; provincial quota table and revised 1947-48 shipping schedule for a national reserve.

sections.title: Problems of Collection
sections.summary: National Food Administration report on Cholla-pukto: too few inspectors, tire and battery shortages, straw bags; Cholla-namdo at 64 per cent on 28 November.

sections.title: Section 2. Prices
sections.summary: New monthly retail price indexes for 26 commodities: composite 1,476 in October 1947 against August 1945 = 100; controlled prices, gold price and National Price Administration actions.

sections.title: Price Indexes
sections.summary: Composite index of 1,476 in October, over twice the year-earlier level; polished rice only 6 times its August 1945 price.

sections.title: Actual Prices
sections.summary: Index and average price tables for Seoul and ten-day open-market prices in nine cities, September-November 1947.

sections.title: Controlled Prices
sections.summary: Controlled rice price stable since November 1945, explaining its lower open-market rise; tables on controlled commodity and tobacco prices.

sections.title: Gold
sections.summary: Wholesale gold price rising steadily since April despite illegality of trading, used as a price-trend indicator; tobacco price increase tables.

sections.title: Activities of the National Price Administration
sections.summary: Price settings quoted from weekly reports: rolled barley at 110 won per small mal, imported ginned cotton at 50 won per pound, 60 textile types.

sections.title: Section 3. Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
sections.summary: Livestock markets, seed potatoes, fertilizer receipts of 97,973 tons of ammonium nitrate, cotton and silk, irrigation projects, forestry and fish catch for January-July 1947.

sections.title: Bureau of Agricultural Economics
sections.summary: 1947 production statistics compiled, draft 1948 production plan emphasizing cereals, and extra grain inspectors hired for rice collection.

sections.title: Livestock
sections.summary: 1946 market data (624,595 cattle brought, 346,810 sold), 1,280 work cattle at breeding stations, Seoul Milk Plant receiving 250 gallons daily, race-track bets of 183 million won.

sections.title: Production
sections.summary: Poultry conference at Suwon 27-28 November, swine increases in Kyonggi-do, poor honey output, and arrival of 408 tons of American seed potatoes at Pusan.

sections.title: Agricultural Experiment Station, Suwon
sections.summary: Fruit tree nursery shortage, apple pest damage in Taegu orchards, and fertilizer yield experiments on rice, barley, wheat, soybeans and potatoes.

sections.title: Cotton and Fiber
sections.summary: 23,000 chungbo of cotton lost to floods, 10,900 chungbo hemp quota for 1948, and straw bag movements for fertilizer shipments.

sections.title: Sericulture
sections.summary: October raw silk output of 6,030 kvan, 52,000 kvan of waste silk in stock, and 1947 cocoon collection of 600,000 kvan.

sections.title: Irrigation
sections.summary: Ground-breaking at the Shi Heung tidal reclamation project on 25 November, a technician training school for 60 men, and completion of the Sam Sung project.

sections.title: Korean Agricultural Association
sections.summary: Fertilizer receipts and sales to 1 November, 20,000 tons moved by small boat, and sales receipts of 538 million won.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: Trial arming of 20 forest policemen with U.S. carbines near Seoul and final management rules for vested forest lands.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: 78 million won loan to the Korean Fisheries Corporation for agar-agar producers, Seoul market arrivals, and January-July 1947 catch table.

sections.title: Section 4. Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: Coal stockpiles falling despite higher output, bituminous coal wholly imported from Japan, a mill fire at Sangdong, an explosion killing four at Chang Hang, and metals production tables.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Coal situation more acute: November mining rose but mine stockpiles declined, signaling approaching exhaustion.

sections.title: Coal
sections.summary: Anthracite and lignite output up 75 and 100 per cent over August, truck tire shortages, Hwasun at 400 tons daily, 55,600 tons of anthracite shipped against 115,000 required.

sections.title: Pitch
sections.summary: Briquette production falling for lack of coal-tar pitch; asphaltic pitch being tested; no control over briquette factories at end-November.

sections.title: Metals
sections.summary: 2 November fire at Sangdong mill, copper cost surveys, explosion killing four at Chang Hang smelter, and May-October tables for gold, silver, copper, tungsten, graphite, zinc, lead.

sections.title: Section 5. Industrial Production
sections.summary: October flour output of 3,208 tons from imported wheat, cotton and paper output, nails near 200 tons, cement, rubber, ginseng purchase of 141,336 cha, and tobacco output up 14 per cent.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Data remain inadequate, covering mainly major vested and Korean-owned factories receiving allocated raw materials.

sections.title: Processed Food
sections.summary: Flour production in two vested mills rose from 430 to 3,208 tons using imported wheat; noodle output fell 38 per cent; Tong-A Food Company output.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: Cotton yarn and cloth rose after 20,000 bales of cotton were imported, though still below October 1946; 4,097 meters of mixed cloth.

sections.title: Paper
sections.summary: Machine-made paper fell about 55 tons from September's high because of coal scarcity; Puksan mill shut for repairs.

sections.title: Hardware
sections.summary: Nail production approached 200 metric tons for the first time in the 12-month series.

sections.title: Other Industry
sections.summary: Briquettes unchanged, coke declining; Onada Cement 1,414 tons of cement; brick and pottery output up after refractory clay imports; rubber items declined.

sections.title: Monopoly Bureau Products
sections.summary: 141,336 cha of ginseng bought for 77 million won, salt output limited by winter, tobacco up 14 per cent with 600 per cent gain over 1945, Chonju factories consolidated.

sections.title: Section 6. Allocation and Distribution
sections.summary: Allocation tables for cloth, shoes, soap, tires and beer; Civilian Supply allocations by agency; Materials Control Corporation stocks; FFA and FDA purchases; petroleum and salt.

sections.title: Allocations, Korean Produced Commodities
sections.summary: Cotton cloth allocations dropped almost 40 per cent while finished goods rose; shoe allocations increased and soap and matches rose; tables July 1946-November 1947.

sections.title: Allocations of Civilian Supplies
sections.summary: Allocations of 44 fire trucks, 1,863 tons of crude rubber, 6,000 radios, steel landing strips, tents and textile dyes to named departments.

sections.title: Allocations, Materials Control Corporation
sections.summary: Allocation of former Japanese Army stocks including 1,000 pounds of Chinese nickel coins and 2 tons of bismuth; inspection of MCC stockpiles near Seoul.

sections.title: Distribution, Korean Produced Commodities
sections.summary: FFA spent 119.6 million won on commodities in November, up 69 per cent; FDA spent 13.8 million won, down 77 per cent.

sections.title: Petroleum
sections.summary: Return of empty drums (85,405 returned against 75,519 delivered) and doubled November kerosene allocation for seasonal demand.

sections.title: Salt
sections.summary: Kimchi-season salt distribution continued, with the full 2.7 kg ration reached in Chunchon, Yongwol and Kangnung by mid-November.

sections.title: Section 7. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Department Order No. 2 on won proceeds of imports, October private imports of 542 million won, trade with Japan, Hong Kong and Egypt, and Civilian Supply imports of coal, fertilizer and food.

sections.title: Private Trade
sections.summary: Order No. 2 requires import won proceeds deposited at the Korea Foreign Exchange Bank; November estimate imports 303.7 million won against exports 221.5 million; October imports a record 542 million won.

sections.title: Trade with United States
sections.summary: Three American trading company representatives visited Korea; payments for July shipments redirected to the National City Bank of New York.

sections.title: Trade with Japan
sections.summary: Shipments September-November, SCAP declining some goods and 1,000 tons of anchovies, and acceptance of 100 tons of lead ingots at $286.60 per ton.

sections.title: Trade with Hong Kong
sections.summary: SS Cannonbar sailed 26 November with fluorspar, silk waste and canned fish; purchase of 400 bales of Indian cotton at $0.2475 per pound.

sections.title: Trade with Egypt
sections.summary: 1,000 bales of raw cotton shipped on the Leopold Skirk toward 3,000 bales bartered in August.

sections.title: Korean Items for Americans in Korea
sections.summary: Souvenir sales through Army Post Exchange delivered $16,548.25 in November, credited to the Department of Commerce.

sections.title: Imports, Civilian Supply
sections.summary: GARIOA and FLC import values, tonnage, 12,391.9 tons of salt in October, 62,517 tons of Japanese coal in November, ammonium nitrate request of 69,663 tons, foodstuff imports.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Wage study of 14 controlled factories, Pusan stevedores after the Chung Pyung arrests, Seoul Electric union-management council, Yong Wol mine wage dispute, child labor and maximum-hours enforcement.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Department of Labor continued work in labor education, industrial health and union-management relations.

sections.title: Wages
sections.summary: Study of wages in 14 controlled Seoul and Yong Dong Po factories; Pusan stevedores shifted from the leftist Chung Pyung union after August arrests.

sections.title: Labor Union Activities
sections.summary: First Seoul Electric Company Union-Management Council met 18 November under the August contract with the Tai Han No Chung Union.

sections.title: Labor Education
sections.summary: Yong Wol mine wage dispute, 5,000-copy Labor News, Tai Han Labor College lectures, and 157 reported maximum-hours complaints of which only 2 were prosecuted.

sections.title: Industrial Health
sections.summary: Factory immunization, inspection of 8 plants with over 1,500 workers, and opening on 10 November of a Seoul Electric hospital building for Constabulary and Coast Guard.

sections.title: Part III. Public Services
sections.summary: Transportation hit by coal shortage (58 trains removed), communications revenue after 1 October rate rises, power deficit, public works and refugee housing.

sections.title: Section 1. Transportation
sections.summary: Department revenue in October highest since April 1946, record railroad freight and coal burn of 62,520 tons, 46 marine vessels, new Yosu port authority, and 58 trains cancelled in November.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: 58 trains removed from service in November for lack of coal; effects to show in next month's statistics.

sections.title: Revenue and Expenditures
sections.summary: October revenue up 19 per cent over September, expenditures down 11 per cent because September included a three-month Japanese coal bill.

sections.title: Railroads
sections.summary: Income, record passenger and freight volumes (heavy rice-buying travel), locomotive availability, repairs of 236 freight cars, employment and wages, and coal consumption.

sections.title: Marine Transportation
sections.summary: Bureau controls 46 vessels (8 Baltic Coasters, 34 LSTs, 5 FS vessels); income rising since April; Korean seamen employment expanding.

sections.title: Highway Transportation
sections.summary: Bureau has no income and is subsidized; 15 November Yosu port authority, Mukko port working well, Kunsan barge shortage.

sections.title: Air Transportation
sections.summary: Bureau still in planning stage with watchmen at seven airfields, no planes, and a small, declining staff.

sections.title: Section 2. Communications
sections.summary: Income flat in October with telephone rates raised 2.5 to 4 times on 1 October, rising expenditures, postal savings and insurance, telephone repairs, and postal orders for China and Japan.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Department of Communications runs postal, telephone, telegraph and radio services, postal insurance and certain banking functions.

sections.title: Revenue and Expenditures
sections.summary: Revenue steady; 1 October telephone, stamp and telegraph rate increases; expenditures up for salaries, travel (per diem 175 to 300 won) and land costs, with 2,000 poles set.

sections.title: Employment
sections.summary: Permanent employment continued to decline in October; table of government income turned over to the Department of Finance.

sections.title: Special Functions
sections.summary: Government income collected for Finance fell 11 per cent from September to October.

sections.title: Postal Deposits and Insurance
sections.summary: Postal savings deposits rose slightly, book transfer deposits rose some 30 million won, and policyholders fell though insurance in force rose 3 per cent.

sections.title: Telephone and Telegraph
sections.summary: Telephone receipts up 174 per cent in October on new rates; telegrams up 17 and 14 per cent.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Repeater station repairs, Yong San exchange inspection of 14 November, Fiscal Bureau voucher system, and Orders 15 and 23 on postal service with China and Japan.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Utilities
sections.summary: Power supply crisis: load of 162,000 kw on 10 November against 105,000 available, 63.2 million KWH from the North, hydro plants idled by low water, plus electric company finance tables.

sections.title: Electricity
sections.summary: Eight plants' status, Seoul and Pusan thermal plants lacking 13,000 tons of coal monthly, Chung Pyung nearly stopped, and North Korean supply of 135,000 kw at peak with 63.2 million KWH for the month.

sections.title: Streetcars
sections.summary: 129 to 135 Seoul streetcars in use carrying 450,000 to 500,000 passengers daily.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Utilities Bureau items: Seoul Electric hospital opened, Pusan steam plant fired, 700 tons of Japanese coal arranged, and a 19 November power-rationing plan.

sections.title: Revenue and Expenditures
sections.summary: Revenue and expense tables for Korea Electric Power, South Korea Electric and Seoul Electric companies.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Works
sections.summary: Man-days and wage spending down about 25 per cent for winter, Andong and Kyopchong bridge contracts, Seoul-Pusan highway paving, water works needs, and Fire Prevention Week 3-8 November.

sections.title: Man-Days and Expenditures
sections.summary: Man-days and wages dropped about 25 per cent from October as winter approached.

sections.title: Roads and Bridges
sections.summary: Contracts let for the 18-span Andong Bridge and others (Kotang 3.4 million won); asphalt paving half done between Yong Dong Po and Amyang.

sections.title: Flood Control and Water Supply
sections.summary: Kun Nam Je levee work from 20 November, five river projects done in Kyongsang-pukto, and Han River-Ascom City water project jobs completed.

sections.title: Urban Water Supply
sections.summary: Inspection of Pusan, Chinhae, Masan, Kosong, Tongyang and Chinju waterworks; Masan limited to 8 hours daily service.

sections.title: Geodetic Survey
sections.summary: Resurveys of Inchon and Sosa completed and map copper plates received from Japan.

sections.title: Fire Control
sections.summary: Fire Prevention Week 3-8 November, poster prize on 29 November, and allocation of 44 fire trucks and 325 pumps received through USOCS.

sections.title: Section 5. Housing
sections.summary: Forty-house low-cost project 50 per cent complete, 400 Seoul houses nearly all occupied, 100 million won refugee housing plan, and refugee-built An Chang Ho and quonset villages.

sections.title: Low Cost Housing
sections.summary: National Housing Administration's forty-house project begun in November, 20 houses erected, for Koreans evicted for American personnel housing.

sections.title: Seoul Housing Project
sections.summary: Nearly all 400 city-built houses occupied; 60 held in reserve but families allowed in temporarily.

sections.title: Refugee Housing
sections.summary: 1947-48 Welfare Housing Plan (100 million won, 24 million for winterized tents), provincial progress table, and 90 per cent of 400 Refugee Shelter Construction Society houses done.

sections.title: Cooperative Villages
sections.summary: An Chang Ho refugee village of 25 buildings west of Seoul, and a quonset hut village for 660 people with orphanage and match factory.

sections.title: Part IV. Finance
sections.summary: Government finance (note issue up 9.2 billion won, budget 45 per cent above last year) and non-government finance (deposits, loans, insurance, bank statistics).

sections.title: Section 1. Government Finance
sections.summary: Largest monthly note issue increase since August 1946, 302 million won excess withdrawals, supplementary budgets for tobacco (569.8 million won) and flood repair, and revenue at 66 per cent of budget.

sections.title: Note Issue of the Bank of Chosun
sections.summary: Note issue rose 9.2 billion won in November, driven by rice-collection credit (12 billion won lines) and deficit spending.

sections.title: Overdrafts and Revenue Deposits
sections.summary: SKIG deposited 917 million won of revenue and withdrew 1,219 million won, an excess withdrawal of 302 million won; tobacco purchases also expanded issue.

sections.title: Expenditure Budget of the South Korean Interim Government
sections.summary: Budget of 17,720,227,310 won approved 2 July; November supplements of 89.5 million (Transportation) and 569.8 million won (Monopoly Bureau); 18 requests over 2,722 million pending.

sections.title: Total Adjusted Expenditures of the South Korean Interim Government, Fiscal Year 1946-47
sections.summary: Table of adjusted expenditures chargeable to 1946/47 through 30 September 1947.

sections.title: Comparison of Total Adjusted Expenditures for Fiscal Year 1946-47 and Total Expenditure Budget for Fiscal Year 1947-48
sections.summary: Budget up over 45 per cent; Transportation, Civil Service, Internal Security, Agriculture and Monopoly Bureau show major increases, National Food Administration a 2,777 million won decrease.

sections.title: Per Capita Expenditure for Fiscal Year 1946-47
sections.summary: On 20 million population, per capita spending was 668.91 won in 1946/47 against 972.26 won proposed for 1947/48.

sections.title: Monthly Receipts and Payments
sections.summary: October expenditures rose 1,553 million won (Monopoly Bureau 1,123 million, Education 398 million); revenue rose led by Monopoly Bureau (449 million).

sections.title: Comparison of Monthly Average of Projected Revenues for Fiscal Year 1947-48 and Monthly Average Collection
sections.summary: Average collection was 70 per cent of projected revenue April-August; improved by end October on Monopoly and tax receipts.

sections.title: Relationship Between Revenue Collections and Approved Budget
sections.summary: Collections at 66 per cent of proposed monthly average expenditures at end October, up from 61 per cent at end September.

sections.title: Taxation
sections.summary: Tax investigators' training school opening in December and new Beverage Tax Ordinance effective 1 November.

sections.title: Delinquent Taxes Due From Vested Properties
sections.summary: 328,284,073 won of assessed national taxes unpaid by vested properties at 31 May 1947; conferences held on collection.

sections.title: Civilian Supply Program
sections.summary: Office of Civilian Supply receipts and disbursements; surplus funds rose over 371 million won in November.

sections.title: Section 2. Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: Seven banks and 142 Financial Associations with 577 branches; October deposits up 2,282 million won, loans up 1,733 million won, insurance growth, and a 3 billion won deposit campaign.

sections.title: Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Seven banks and 142 Financial Associations had 577 branches; FFA headquarters in Seoul with branches in nine provincial capitals.

sections.title: Cash Balances in Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Cash balances fell 175 million won in October amid payments to farmers for rice, tobacco, straw products and seed cotton.

sections.title: Deposits in Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Deposit balances rose 2,282 million won (7 per cent); government deposits up 3,420 million, inter-bank down 1,088 million, public down 50 million, the first public decline since January.

sections.title: Deposit Balance of Each Financial Institution
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun up 2,322 million won, Financial Associations up 350 million, Mutual Aid Bank up 18 million; five other banks down 408 million.

sections.title: Loans by Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Net loan balance rose 1,733 million won (12 per cent): government guaranteed loans up 711 million, others 1,022 million, mainly for seed cotton, rice and straw products.

sections.title: Analysis of Loans Made by Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Industrial Bank held 28 per cent of loans, Bank of Chosun 25 per cent; 16,067 million won approved 5 May-18 November, 97 per cent for government policy.

sections.title: Life Insurance
sections.summary: Insurance in force up 45 million won (11 per cent) and monthly premiums up nearly 40 per cent in October.

sections.title: Damage Insurance
sections.summary: Liabilities assumed up 1,005 million won (75 per cent) and premiums up 55 per cent, the largest rises since April 1946.

sections.title: Activities of Financial Institutions
sections.summary: November loans including 150 million won for straw bags, bank shareholder meetings, precious-metals sale license, 3 billion won deposit drive, and destruction of 400 million yen of Bank of Japan notes.

sections.title: Activities of Life and Damage Insurance Companies
sections.summary: 95 policies reinsured for 9.675 million yen, 561,551 policyholders with claims on Japanese insurers, and a 40 million won risk on the Chosun Printing Plant.

sections.title: Other Financial Statistics
sections.summary: Tables 15-19: Bank of Chosun interest rates, assets and liabilities of each bank, and clearing house transactions.

sections.title: Part V. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Dean's inauguration, election and UN issues, executive-legislature friction, KILA debate on the Outline, party maneuvering, legal ordinances, police history, and interzone monitoring.

sections.title: Section 1. Administration
sections.summary: Dean inaugurated 3 November; Hodge and Dean refuse an early election; Helmick returns KILA measures; National Police Board created under Ordinance 157; National Economic Board handles power and budget.

sections.title: Inauguration of Military Governor
sections.summary: Dean replaces the late Maj. Gen. Lerch on 3 November and states three U.S. aims: independent Korea, democratic government, sound economy and education.

sections.title: Election Under United Nations
sections.summary: Hodge's 19 November statement and Dean's 27 November release refusing an election before the UN Commission arrives; 15-member Election Committee met 18 November.

sections.title: Relations Between the Executive and the Assembly
sections.summary: Helmick's replies on frozen yen, a delegation to Japan, UN representatives, two-thirds confirmation rule, and temple property; Dean's Ordinance 153; Public Prostitution Law signed 14 November.

sections.title: Korea Civil Service
sections.summary: Statistics course in its tenth week, training officers in each province, and CAF 10-13 clerk examinations in Kyongsang-pukto.

sections.title: National Police Board
sections.summary: Ordinance 157 board appointed 25 November with six members to rule on senior police appointments and appeals.

sections.title: National Economic Board
sections.summary: Meetings of 10, 18 and 25 November approved supplemental budgets, reviewed the Sumgin Gang dam, and recommended emergency power measures and payment for North Korean power.

sections.title: Section 2. Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: 13 sessions averaging 65 members; six on the Outline; Temporary Entertainment Law passed; Ordinance 153 amended; Dean's 10 November speech; Helmick's letters on constitution and collaborators bill.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: 13 November sessions, average attendance 65 and length 3.5 hours; Outline, entertainment law and an executive-legislative misunderstanding.

sections.title: Outline of Measures for Meeting the Current Situation in South Korea
sections.summary: Directors Ahn and Chough questioned on 7 November; 'sovereign' wording and leftist objections; KILA split on a no-confidence demand, then rejection motions failing 32-20 and 33-20.

sections.title: Temporary Law for Cessation of Professional Entertainment Activities
sections.summary: Law suspending high-class restaurants, bars, cabarets, dance halls and licensed kisaeng; second reading 24 November, third reading waived 48-0.

sections.title: Ordinance No. 153
sections.summary: Ordinance 153 on aiding American personnel to violate military directives; first reading 6 November; text and later wording changes.

sections.title: Speech by General Dean
sections.summary: Dean addressed KILA on 10 November, urging executive-legislative cooperation and praising its legislative record.

sections.title: Letters from Executive Branch
sections.summary: Helmick's letters on Kangwon-do and Chungchong-namdo governors, UN representative, frozen yen, and withholding of the Temporary Constitution and collaborators' law, angering some members.

sections.title: Section 3. Political Developments
sections.summary: Full text of the Outline and reactions; three groups on independence (UN election, immediate election under Rhee, Council of 12 Parties); Dean's reception; party anniversaries.

sections.title: Outline of Measures for Meeting the Current Situation in South Korea
sections.summary: Quotes Part II of the 25 September Outline, including its views on sovereignty and U.S. withdrawal conditions, and protests by leftists, the National Society and rightist parties.

sections.title: Independence and Unification
sections.summary: Moderates back UN-observed elections; Rhee demands elections by mid-December; the Council of 12 Parties' four-point program, defections by Korean Democratic and Hankook parties, and loss of power.

sections.title: Military Governor
sections.summary: Dean received with courteous but pointedly qualified reception by most political factions at his 3 November inauguration.

sections.title: Organizations and Anniversaries
sections.summary: Korean Democratic Party's second anniversary 3 November, South Korea Labor Party's first on 23 November, and Hong Myawng Hi elected chairman of the Democratic Independence Party.

sections.title: Section 4. Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Ordinances 149 and 153-156 including the Beverage Tax Law, Public Act No. 7 abolishing licensed prostitution, legal opinions, 21,372 prisoners, and Han Chi Keun's life sentence for the Lyuh Woon Hyong assassination.

sections.title: Functions of Department of Justice
sections.summary: Department frames ordinances and orders, renders legality opinions, and assists court modernization.

sections.title: Ordinances and Orders
sections.summary: Executive Order 7 closing Haibang News Agency, Ordinances 149, 153, 154 (Beverage Tax with rates and license fees), 155 and 156, Communications Orders 22-23, Public Act No. 7.

sections.title: Legal Opinions
sections.summary: Opinions on foreigners' land purchase and national defense areas, validity of a Korean-American soldier's marriage, and Chungang Pharmaceutical's bismuth claim.

sections.title: Penal Institutions
sections.summary: 17 prisons and 6 work camps held 21,372 prisoners at 30 November; 202 boys moved from Kumchon to Inchon Boys' Prison.

sections.title: Korean Courts
sections.summary: Conference on the Court Reorganization Law dispute between judges and Justice Department officials, week ending 8 November.

sections.title: Claims Bureau
sections.summary: Han Chi Keun sentenced to life for assassinating Lyuh Woon Hyong; Claims Bureau handles claims against SKIG and vested property claims.

sections.title: Section 5. Police
sections.summary: Department of Police summary of Japanese-era police powers, approximately 580 women police, Ordinance 157 police board, crime laboratory and 15,118 fingerprint requests, new Police Welfare Association.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Month's report gives background material instead of statistics, including practices under the Japanese and work for women.

sections.title: Administration of Justice Under Japanese
sections.summary: Department of Police account of colonial police powers, six departments including censorship and thought control, absence of civil rights, and attitudes of people, police and officials.

sections.title: Police Women
sections.summary: About 580 policewomen, mostly in Seoul, Taegu, Inchon and Pusan, trained four weeks and deployed for juvenile and female cases.

sections.title: Organizational Changes
sections.summary: National Police Board under Ordinance 157 and another reorganization of police powers.

sections.title: Crime Laboratory
sections.summary: Equipment, ballistics, handwriting and photography units; 22 detective cases referred, 20 completed, 15,118 fingerprint requests answered.

sections.title: Police Welfare Association
sections.summary: Association formed in the first week of November and began negotiating with the welfare bureau for UNRRA clothing.

sections.title: Section 6. Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Alternate-Saturday mail exchanges at Tosong and monitoring of Radio Pyongyang: Kim Il Sung's 2 November anniversary speech, rice price claims, education, Soviet films and wheat planting.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Report incomplete for security reasons, covering mail exchanges and Radio Pyongyang intercepts.

sections.title: Mail Exchange
sections.summary: Mail exchanged between North and South on alternate Saturdays at Tosong, with November counts by date.

sections.title: North Korean Radio
sections.summary: Kim Il Sung blamed the U.S. for the Joint Commission's failure; Pyongyang cited South Korean rice price rises, 286 Soviet films, literacy gains and wheat planting over quota.

sections.title: Part VI. Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education with the New Education Exhibit, culture and radio, public information, press and public opinion, and Korean National Youth.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Vital statistics planning, one more cholera death (10 in 1947), plague control program, X-ray machines, laboratories and biologicals, narcotics licenses, refugee camp winterization and Women's Center.

sections.title: Vital Statistics
sections.summary: Plans for birth, death, marriage and morbidity statistics from 1 January 1948; 16,854 marriages and 1,280 divorces April-December 1946.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: Tenth cholera death of 1947 in Hyopchon, communicable disease drop, smallpox and typhus vaccination of children, 56,894 rats killed in Cheju-do, plague control program.

sections.title: Medical Services
sections.summary: Five U.S. X-ray machines distributed, six leper clinics, and the unheated Women's Medical College with 500 students.

sections.title: Nursing Affairs
sections.summary: Four-day course for 62 public health nurses, Helmick at graduation of 20 nurses on 4 November, 1,214 midwives and 1,261 nurses registered.

sections.title: Dental Affairs
sections.summary: Seoul National University Dental College moved to the Department of Education and the American dental advisory section discontinued.

sections.title: Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: Animal hospital construction begun, anthrax deaths of 8 cattle in Kyongsang-pukto, and 58 horses for the police quarantined at Pusan.

sections.title: Laboratories
sections.summary: Survey of seven provincial laboratories, plague vaccine study after a case near the Manchurian border, and tables on biologicals.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical Affairs
sections.summary: Tables on Korean, American and veterinary biologicals and 2,526 narcotic licenses issued since August 1945.

sections.title: Public Assistance
sections.summary: Welfare institution survey, winterization of nine camps along the 38th parallel, 300 blankets to Chunchon, Red Cross clothing plan.

sections.title: Women's Bureau
sections.summary: Women's Center took over the former Hokuksa building, child-training meetings 15-17 November, and first sub-section heads' meeting 13-14 November.

sections.title: Section 2. Education
sections.summary: New Education Exhibit (21 November-5 December, 104,976 visitors), founding of the Association of Colleges and Universities on 28 November, supplies for normal schools, and Education Director Yu Uck Kyum's death on 8 November.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Exhibit as focal point of educational activity and large contributions to education.

sections.title: New Education Exhibit
sections.summary: First national exhibit at Seoul Middle School with 104,976 visitors; seven educator conferences; 105 top education donors honored 23 November.

sections.title: Korean Association of Colleges and Universities
sections.summary: All 29 college presidents and deans founded the association on 28 November, with officers from Seoul National and Korea universities; tables of approved institutions.

sections.title: Technological Training Board
sections.summary: Board approved training projects in November; table of other universities and colleges.

sections.title: Conference of Educational Leaders
sections.summary: American national and provincial education advisers met in Seoul 31 October-1 November.

sections.title: Supplies for Teacher Training
sections.summary: Notebooks and light bulbs from Civilian Supplies distributed to normal schools; American professional books received.

sections.title: Oratorical Contest
sections.summary: 27 students from 12 colleges entered the English oratorical contest ending 29 November at Seoul National University.

sections.title: Death of Director of Education, Yu, Uck Kyum
sections.summary: Yu Uck Kyum died 8 November aged 53; appointed Education Director 19 December 1945.

sections.title: Section 3. Culture
sections.summary: Introduction to Korean art, Korean United Fine Arts Exhibition 9-30 November, chrysanthemum show with 27,684 visitors, YWCA, Korean Broadcasting System programming and a musical contest.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Quotations from Andreas Eckardt's History of Korean Art and notes on museums, music and dance.

sections.title: Korean United Fine Arts Exhibition
sections.summary: Held at Kyung Bok Palace 9-30 November from over 300 entries, with 63 Western and 24 Oriental paintings.

sections.title: Chrysanthemum Exhibition
sections.summary: 250 chrysanthemums at Duk Soo Palace, 23 October-25 November, 27,684 visitors and 259,109 won in fees.

sections.title: Altrusa Club and YWCA
sections.summary: Altrusa Club meetings and 22 November report on the Hangchow YWCA World Council with nine Korean delegates.

sections.title: YWCA in South Korea
sections.summary: Seoul Central YWCA with nearly 2,000 members, three schools, 14 city and rural associations and 28 student associations.

sections.title: Korean Broadcasting System
sections.summary: Seoul station plus nine affiliates, 10.5 hour daily schedule; children's, women's, educational, drama, music and religious programs; typical 17 November schedule and November breakdown.

sections.title: Musical Contest
sections.summary: Second yearly contest held 6 November under the Bureau of Culture, with prizes awarded 18 November.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Information
sections.summary: Press releases on Civilian Supply, refugees, forests and Ordinance 153, Farmers Weekly (300,000 circulation), opinion sampling, publication licensing, and a Chunchon mobile education trip.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Department of Public Information informs Koreans of government and world events and gauges opinion, with the Office of Civil Information.

sections.title: Bureau of Public Information
sections.summary: Press releases on USOCS, New Korea Company advances, migration figures, forest theft, a narcotics factory seizure, 170 price-ceiling prosecutions; special releases and Farmers Weekly.

sections.title: Bureau of Public Opinion
sections.summary: 15 party registrations received, publication licensing figures, four opinion samplings, 20 illustrated lectures, translation of 25 editorials and political education work.

sections.title: Motion Picture Section
sections.summary: Work described under Culture.

sections.title: Radio Bureau
sections.summary: Political broadcasts including a Labor Department speech and talk on Korean National Youth.

sections.title: Office of Civil Information
sections.summary: Mobile Education train in Chunchon 7-10 November; of 290 questioned, 38.6 per cent read Farmers Weekly, 88.4 per cent of those liking it.

sections.title: Section 5. Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Korean press reaction to Dean's inauguration, the Political Affairs Council Outline, 12-party talks and Rhee's election demands, the governor's vetoes and a court-jurisdiction dispute, plus a monthly opinion poll.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Press focused on Dean's inauguration, the Political Affairs Council document and UN developments.

sections.title: Inauguration of the Military Governor, Major General William F. Dean
sections.summary: Dae Han Ilbo and Dong-A Ilbo editorials urged Dean to complete transfer of administration to Koreans and hoped he would be the last military governor.

sections.title: Political Affairs Council
sections.summary: Press attacks on the Outline; Seoul Shin Mun on 11 November called its spirit anti-national and impure.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Interest in the 12-party conferences, Hodge's 19 November election statement and Rhee's widely quoted attack on treatment of Koreans.

sections.title: The Governor and KILA
sections.summary: Conflict over the governor's vetoes prompted press debate on whether KILA should disband.

sections.title: The Governor and the Courts
sections.summary: Outcry over transfer of a political murder case to the Provost Marshal's court; three Court of Appeals judges threatened to resign; Dean's 1 December release.

sections.title: Public Opinion
sections.summary: Party demands and a Korean Patriotic Women's Alliance poll on UN success, Soviet-American withdrawal, and the newspaper law.

sections.title: Section 6. Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: Membership of about 350,000 (70,000 in the Sea Youth) more than doubled in four months; community programs, Suwon training conferences, rivalry with Dai Dong, and a hostel for officials.

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Organization promotes democratic procedures and gains in numbers and prestige despite conflict.

sections.title: Membership
sections.summary: More than doubled in four months to 350,000, including 70,000 in Korean National Sea Youth.

sections.title: The Program
sections.summary: Discussion groups, literacy classes, tree planting, road repair and farm help; women's section teaches home nursing and crafts.

sections.title: Training
sections.summary: Four weekly Suwon training conferences for chiefs; 196 Organization and 216 Activities trainees graduated.

sections.title: Opposition
sections.summary: Rivalry with the rightist Dai Dong youth group eased; Dai Dongs accused of tearing down posters and coercing members.

sections.title: Continued Activities
sections.summary: Repair of a former Constabulary building as a hostel for visiting officials and dormitory for refugee students.
